summary: Configured PostgreSQL 13 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, and node3 (standbys) on AlmaLinux 9, secured with a self-signed CA (CN=postgres-cluster-ca) created on node1. Per-node server certs (CN=node1/node2/node3) and a replicator client cert (CN=replicator) were issued by that CA and distributed. pg_hba.conf on all nodes restricts replication to hostssl entries requiring `cert` auth (clientcert=verify-full implied), so only peers presenting a CA-issued client cert can replicate; plaintext and foreign-CA-signed connections were proven to fail. Standbys were built via pg_basebackup -R over TLS (sslmode=verify-full) and are streaming with TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol (standbys first, primary last), proving changed boot IDs on every node and confirming post-restart replication/data recovery, including a live write on the primary after its own restart.
actions_performed: Inspected all three nodes (AlmaLinux 9.6, no PostgreSQL pre-installed, root access, firewalld active)
Installed postgresql-server 13.23 + contrib + openssl on node1, node2, node3
Created a self-signed CA on node1 (/opt/pg-ca/ca.key, ca.crt, CN=postgres-cluster-ca, 10y validity)
Issued CA-signed server certs for node1/node2/node3 (CN=<node>, SAN DNS+IP) and a client cert for CN=replicator
Set up cluster SSH between nodes using CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY and distributed CA cert + node certs/keys via scp to /opt/pg-ca on node2/node3
Initialized PGDATA on node1 via postgresql-setup --initdb, installed server.crt/server.key/ca.crt with correct ownership/permissions
Configured postgresql.conf (ssl on, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders/replication_slots) and pg_hba.conf (hostssl replication replicator <ip>/32 cert) on node1
Created replicator role with REPLICATION LOGIN privilege
Opened port 5432/tcp in firewalld on all three nodes
Copied CA cert + replicator client cert/key to /var/lib/pgsql/certs (0600 key, postgres-owned) on node2 and node3
Ran pg_basebackup -R with PGSSLMODE=verify-full and client cert env vars on node2 and node3 to clone from node1 and auto-generate primary_conninfo with sslmode=verify-full and cert paths
Installed each standby's own server cert/key/ca.crt, added ssl config and hot_standby=on, plus hostssl replication ... cert entries on node2/node3
Started and enabled postgresql service on node1, node2, node3
Verified pg_stat_replication shows both standbys streaming over TLS (TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384) via pg_stat_ssl
Verified data written on primary replicates to both standbys (matching LSN and row contents)
Proved a self-signed (non-CA) client cert is rejected at TLS handshake ('unknown ca')
Proved a plaintext (sslmode=disable) replication attempt from node2 is rejected by pg_hba.conf with 'SSL off' error
Captured baseline boot_id and health (replication/recovery status, table contents) on all three nodes
Restarted node2 via `reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed postgresql active, standby caught up in recovery, and primary shows it streaming again
Restarted node3 via `reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed recovery and data intact, confirmed rejoined replication on primary

Restarted node1 (primary) last via `reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed postgresql active and not in recovery, performed a new write, confirmed both standbys received it over TLS

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication configured node1 (primary) -> node2, node3
evidence.summary: pg_basebackup -R cloned node2/node3 from node1; both started as standbys and pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both walreceivers 'streaming'/async; a row inserted on primary appeared on both standbys at matching LSN

evidence.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a cluster-created CA
evidence.summary: CA created on node1 (CN=postgres-cluster-ca); server certs per node and a replicator client cert issued by that CA; pg_stat_ssl on primary shows both replication connections using ssl=t with cipher TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384

evidence.requirement: Only peers presenting a CA-issued certificate are accepted for replication
evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf restricts replication to 'hostssl replication replicator <ip>/32 cert'; a self-signed (non-CA) client cert was rejected with 'SSL error: tlsv1 alert unknown ca', and a plaintext attempt from node2 was rejected with 'no pg_hba.conf entry ... SSL off'

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 8c28f3cd...; reboot acked and connection dropped (timeout); post-reboot boot_id bba87b59... (changed); postgresql active, not in recovery, accepted a new write, and both standbys received it over TLS

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e65e6bcf...; reboot acked and connection reset; post-reboot boot_id 24ca4209... (changed); postgresql active, still in recovery with prior data intact, and primary shows it streaming again

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 54089086...; reboot acked and connection reset; post-reboot boot_id d6156164... (changed); postgresql active, still in recovery with prior data intact, and primary shows it streaming again
